findings.reason: The protected implementation is concise, conventional Huffman-style greedy code suitable for an expert interview. The heap imports make minimum-pair selection explicit, while `combined` and `total` name the only evolving values beyond the in-place heap. The loop exposes the singleton boundary naturally, and there is no prohibited local `index`, unnecessary abstraction, code golf, or obscure library trick. No material improvement warrants a candidate.

Each original length contributes once for every ancestor merge in the binary merge tree. Exchanging deeper leaves with larger shallower leaves cannot reduce the cost, so the two smallest current lengths can be deepest siblings in some optimum and may be merged first. Charging their sum and reinserting the combined stick leaves the same optimization problem on a smaller collection. Repeating that choice therefore reaches a global optimum; one stick correctly requires zero merges.

A memoized exact oracle tried every possible pair merge for all 791 nondecreasing multisets of lengths 1 through 7 with values 1 through 5. Protected and immutable native sources matched every global optimum. A separately structured repeated-sort control agreed with all 9 authored cases, all three benchmark outputs, and another 10,000 deterministic random arrays generated with seed 1167, including singleton, pair, tie-heavy, unbalanced, unsorted, and maximum-value inputs.

The implementation intentionally heapifies `sticks` in place and reuses that list for all removals and insertions. Every merge decreases its length by one, so no input-sized auxiliary collection is created and the stated O(1) auxiliary-space convention is accurate. The Approach clearly discloses this mutation and the O(n)-space copy alternative.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1167, Python, and native entrypoint Solution.connectSticks. Authenticated source evidence confirms positive integer lengths, arbitrary pair selection, immediate x+y cost, reinsertion of the combined stick, termination at one stick, minimum total, n from 1 through 10^4, and each length from 1 through 10^4. It contains exactly three explained examples, two constraints, and four hints.

The immutable native source remains byte-for-byte bound to verified submission 2067880714. Apart from the required class/method wrapper and List annotation, native and protected sources import the same heap primitives, heapify the input, pop two minima, accumulate and reinsert their sum, terminate at one element, and return the same total. solve.py, leetcode.py, and submission.json were not edited.

The unchanged hidden tiers use 32, 64, and 128 equal-length sticks, a 4x span that forces all n-1 merges with one consistent size meaning. Protected passed every output at a 0.98x largest runtime ratio and -0.02 extra growth exponent. Two independently correct slower controls also passed every output and failed only scaling: repeated sorting at 1.41x/+0.16 and linear minimum selection at 2.23x/+0.27. The evidence supports O(n log n) heap work without changing benchmark.json.

The Approach exactly matches the source's minimum-pair greedy choice, in-place heap construction, two removals, cost accumulation, reinsertion, and one-element termination. It supplies the exchange and reduced-subproblem reasoning, derives O(n log n) time from n-1 heap updates, and explains O(1) auxiliary space through input reuse.

The modular Reference preserves positive stick lengths, arbitrary current-pair choice, sum-based cost and replacement length, continued merging to one stick, minimum-total objective, all three exact examples with every explanatory merge step, both constraints, and all four hints in source order. It introduces no source-absent example, note, follow-up, table, image, or diagram.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed exactly three explained examples, two constraints, four hints, and no source tables, images, or diagrams. source_fidelity.json binds every modular section to live statement hash e23b8934a896a5a401c0706971a82b42a471b15500dbf644b33fb005be0382f3 and validates without errors.

coverage: sample-1, sample-2, and sample-3 are the only authenticated source examples and preserve their exact arrays and outputs. Their explanations retain every source merge, intermediate collection, individual cost, final one-stick state, and total, including the singleton no-operation explanation.

All 9 ordinary fixtures are visible samples or trials. They cover n = 1, n = 2, and n = 10000; stick values 1 and 10000; exactly one merge; equal-minimum ties; a highly unbalanced long stick; unsorted input; and two maximum-length sticks. The 10000-element case independently verifies the maximum-count boundary with total 133616.

A repeated-sort oracle recomputed every authored and benchmark expectation. An exact all-pairs dynamic program covered 791 complete small multisets, and 10,000 deterministic random arrays with seed 1167 covered varied lengths and values. Protected and immutable native sources agreed throughout while each invocation received its own copy because the accepted algorithm deliberately mutates the input list.

The three hidden performance-only tiers use number of sticks consistently as size and span 32 through 128. Protected passed at -0.02 and 0.98x. Repeated-sort and linear-minimum controls passed all 12 ordinary-plus-benchmark outputs and failed only scaling at +0.16/1.41x and +0.27/2.23x respectively. benchmark.json remained unchanged.
